title: Learn HTTP Clients in Go
description: Build requests, inspect responses, decode representations, resolve addresses, and use HTTP tooling safely.

lessons.title: Communicating on the Web
lessons.instruction: Web communication is a request-response exchange: a client asks and a server replies. Complete the round-trip description.

lessons.title: HTTP Requests and Responses
lessons.instruction: An HTTP response separates outcome metadata from its body. Send a GET request to the local server, then print both status and body.
lessons.solution:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
)

func main() {
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprint(w, r.Method) }))
	defer server.Close()
	response, _ := http.Get(server.URL)
	defer response.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(response.Body)
	fmt.Println(response.StatusCode, string(body))
}

lessons.title: Requests and Responses Quiz
lessons.instruction: The request asks for a resource; the response reports the result. Classify the two messages.
lessons.starter:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	request, response := "HTTP/1.1 200 OK", "GET /items HTTP/1.1"
	fmt.Println("request:", request)
	fmt.Println("response:", response)
}
lessons.expected:
request: GET /items HTTP/1.1
response: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
lessons.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	request, response := "GET /items HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"

lessons.title: Web Addresses

lessons.title: Uniform Resource Identifiers

lessons.title: Sections of a URL

lessons.title: The Protocol

lessons.title: URL Ports

lessons.title: Query Parameters

lessons.title: What Are HTTP Headers?
lessons.instruction: HTTP headers carry metadata as case-insensitive names with one or more values. Set and retrieve one with http.Header.

lessons.title: Using the Browser's Developer Tools
lessons.instruction: Print the request detail a browser Network panel exposes: method, path, and request identifier.

lessons.title: Why Are Headers Useful?
lessons.instruction: Accept lets a client state which response media types it understands. Request JSON without changing the URL.
lessons.starter:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
)

func main() {
	handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprint(w, r.Header.Get("Accept")) })
	request := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/profile", nil)
	request.Header.Set("Accept", "text/plain")
	response := httptest.NewRecorder()
	handler.ServeHTTP(response, request)
	fmt.Print(response.Body.String())
}
lessons.solution:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
)

func main() {
	handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprint(w, r.Header.Get("Accept")) })
	request := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/profile", nil)
	request.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
	response := httptest.NewRecorder()
	handler.ServeHTTP(response, request)
	fmt.Print(response.Body.String())
}

lessons.title: POST Requests

lessons.title: RESTful APIs

lessons.title: HTTPS
lessons.instruction: HTTPS is HTTP carried over an authenticated, encrypted TLS connection. Call the trusted local TLS server and print its scheme and status.
lessons.solution:
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
)

func main() {
	server := httptest.NewTLSServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent) }))
	defer server.Close()
	response, _ := server.Client().Get(server.URL)
	defer response.Body.Close()
	u, _ := url.Parse(server.URL)
	fmt.Println(u.Scheme, response.StatusCode)
}
